Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

basemapper 0.1.0

First version, not yet released.

One API across R, Python and Rust

The R and Python packages (and the Rust core’s Basemap) share function names, argument names and defaults; R’s verb(m, ...) is m.verb(...) in Python. See docs/api.md in the repository.

  • Shared arguments: style, width / height (CSS px), center + zoom or bounds + crs, pixel_ratio, layers, auth_token, tile_timeout_ms, max_tiles, tile_concurrency, fail_on_tile_error (default FALSE everywhere), tile_zoom (tile detail override) and path (output file).
  • Providers and list_layers() are implemented once in the Rust core, so both languages return the same styles; list_layers() returns a data frame of id and type in drawing order; list_providers() is new.

Rendering

  • Vector styles are drawn by an in-house CPU port of MapLibre GL JS’s renderer, tested pixel by pixel against MapLibre GL JS (168 reference views: CARTO Positron, Dark Matter and Voyager and the UGRC basemap at zooms 1-22, fractional zoom, pixel ratio 2, OSM raster tiles). No GPU, browser or display is needed; the earlier maplibre-rs/wgpu engine is gone.
  • Basemaps render at any fractional zoom and pixel ratio (MapLibre’s devicePixelRatio): the same view and labels, drawn at the output resolution.
  • Several styles can be stacked bottom to top, e.g. a basemap published as separate hillshade, base and label services.
  • True vector SVG output: fills and lines as paths, icons embedded, labels as editable <text> at MapLibre’s glyph positions with the style’s fonts embedded (subset; open fonts from Google Fonts or your font_dirs), or as traced glyph outlines with render_svg(text = "paths").
  • Views crossing the anti-meridian render MapLibre’s world copies.
  • Tile URLs are requested as MapLibre requests them: all tiles templates (spread over subdomains), scheme: "tms", and the {quadkey}, {prefix}, {ratio} and {bbox-epsg-3857} tokens. wms_style() uses {bbox-epsg-3857} and sends SRS for WMS 1.1.x.

New functions

  • basemap() creates a map view from a centre and zoom or from bounds; set_view() and set_bounds() change it, get_bounds(), get_center(), get_zoom() and get_size() read it.
  • render_png(), render_svg(), render_array() and render_raster() (a terra SpatRaster) render a view.
  • render_basemap_raw(bounds, width, height, style, ...) renders bounds in one call; it accepts stacked styles and pixel_ratio.
  • style accepts tile data as well as styles, building the style for it: a tile URL, TileJSON, PMTiles archive (URL or local file, raster or vector, read from the archive), ArcGIS MapServer or VectorTileServer, or a local style file. Vector data gets a default style drawing every source layer.
  • Styles: basemap_provider() (named catalogue), tile_style() (a style for tile data, with overrides), wms_style() and wmts_style(); list_layers() inspects a style.
  • Named basemaps are a hand-curated catalogue with leaflet-providers names (CartoDB.Positron, Esri.WorldImagery, OpenStreetMap.HOT, plus OpenFreeMap): 42 basemaps, each with a vector form, a raster form or both. A name works as style directly. basemap_provider(name, type, api_key, tiles) picks the form (vector by default; asking for a missing form is an error, never a fallback), reads API keys from CARTO_API_KEY, MAPTILER_API_KEY or STADIA_API_KEY, and draws your own tiles with a basemap’s style. Unknown names suggest close ones. list_providers() returns a data frame of names, forms, key variables and attribution; providers completes names (providers$CartoDB.Positron). CARTO now needs a free API key.
  • Tiles are cached on disk as long as the server’s caching headers allow; tile_cache() shows, moves, disables or clears the cache (in tools::R_user_dir("basemapper", "cache") by default). Requests identify basemapper in their User-Agent.
  • labels and features draw parts of a style, so basemaps can be stacked: labels = FALSE drops the labels, labels = "only" keeps just them on a transparent background, and features keeps (c("water", "roads")) or drops ("-buildings") background, water, landcover, parks, buildings, roads, rail, boundaries, places, poi or terrain. They work on every renderer and plot layer (for the whole stack) and on basemap_provider() (for one basemap, e.g. imagery under a vector basemap’s labels). Features come from tables for the OpenMapTiles, Protomaps and Shortbread schemas and keywords for Esri’s layer names; catalogue raster basemaps switch to their label-free or label-only tiles (CARTO, Esri, Stamen). list_layers() gains a feature column.
  • get_attribution() returns the attribution text a view or style asks maps to show, for a caption: every source’s attribution (from the style, its TileJSON or PMTiles metadata) as plain text, without duplicates.
  • Plot layers (geom_basemap(), tm_basemap(), add_basemap()) draw the basemap’s credit line in the bottom-right corner: attribution = TRUE by default, FALSE to turn it off, or your own text.
  • layers takes * and ? wildcards ("-label_*"). Names in layers or features that match no layer of any style warn.
  • list_layers() shows each layer’s source_layer, and takes layers, labels and features to preview what a render draws.
  • Raster basemaps no longer show a one-pixel white line at tile seams when rendered at a fractional pixel ratio (as a figure’s dpi gives).
  • ArcGIS vector styles whose source names the VectorTileServer without a trailing slash (Esri’s item styles) load their tiles.

Plot layers

  • geom_basemap() renders when the plot is drawn, for the panel’s size at the device’s resolution: ggsave(dpi = 300) gets a basemap rendered at 300 dpi (PDF and SVG devices also use 300 dpi). The pixel ratio defaults to dpi / 96 so lines and labels keep their physical size; pixel_ratio = overrides.
  • tm_basemap() (tmap v4) sizes its basemap from the map panel and device resolution, so tmap_save(dpi = 300) gets a native basemap too.
  • Both accept a vector of styles to stack.
